title: Finite-presentation stalk and compatible fibre quotient data
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $\mathcal F$ be a finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and let $x\in X$, $s=f(x)$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $M=\mathcal F_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and $\alpha=f_x^\sharp:R\to B$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Write $\mathfrak m_R$ for the maximal ideal of $R$, $I=\mathfrak m_RB$ for its extended ideal, and $\mathfrak m_RM=IM$. Let $p:X_s\to X$ be the projection of the scheme-theoretic fibre and $x'\in X_s$ its unique point over $x$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]; put $\mathcal F_s=p^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $\alpha$ is a local homomorphism, and there are a finitely presented $R$-algebra $P$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], a multiplicative subset $T\subseteq P$ and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $T^{-1}P\cong B$. The $B$-module $M$ is finitely presented: there is an exact sequence $B^{\oplus a}\to B^{\oplus b}\to M\to0$ with $a,b\geq0$. There are compatible isomorphisms
$$\theta:B/I\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{X_s,x'},\qquad
\eta:M/\mathfrak m_RM\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathcal F_s)_{x'},$$
where $\theta(\bar b)=p^\sharp_{x'}(b)$ and $\eta$ is additive and $\theta$-semilinear. For every local section $t\in\mathcal F(U)$ with $x\in U$, $\eta(\overline{t_x})=(p^*t)_{x'}$, where $p^*t$ is the section induced by the pullback adjunction unit.

source.place: Tag 080Q, lemma-flat-and-free-at-point-fibre, proof: the local algebra setup for applying the fibre flatness criterion to the identity of X; affine presentations and compatible fibre stalk identifications.

proof.text: The map $\alpha$ is local by the definition of a scheme morphism. Choose affine neighbourhoods $x\in U\subseteq X$, $s\in V\subseteq S$, with $f(U)\subseteq V$ and finitely presented coordinate-ring map, using local finite presentation. The restricted morphism $g:U\to V$ is locally finitely presented: the same affine pair witnesses finite presentation at every point of $U$. Its stalks at $x,s$ identify with $B,R$: restricting neighbourhoods to $U,V$ preserves germs, since a neighbourhood $W$ is replaced by $W\cap U$ or $W\cap V$, and equality of germs is unchanged. The restricted stalk map is $\alpha$, as both send a represented section to the germ of its pullback. Apply the affine stalk localization model to $g,x$. It supplies $R\to P\to B$ and $T\subseteq P$, with $P$ finitely presented over $R$ and $B$ a localization at $T$; the defining universal property of localization gives the required $R$-algebra isomorphism $T^{-1}P\cong B$.

source.place: Tag 080Q, local algebra setup; affine localization model as in Algebra Tags 00R7 and 00RH; open restriction on germs

proof.text: Apply the finite-presentation source-stalk lemma to the ringed space underlying $X$, the finitely presented module sheaf $\mathcal F$, and $x$. Its maps $B^m\xrightarrow{u}B^n\xrightarrow{v}M$ satisfy that $v$ is surjective and $\operatorname{Im}u=\operatorname{Ker}v$. Thus $B^m\to B^n\to M\to0$ is the required exact sequence, with $a=m$, $b=n$ (including either rank zero).

source.place: Tag 01CP, lemma-stalk-internal-hom, third proof paragraph: finite presentation of the source stalk

proof.text: Apply the scheme-fibre stalk quotient lemma to $f,x$. It gives the unique point $x'$ over $x$ and a surjection $q=p^\sharp_{x'}:B\to C=\mathcal O_{X_s,x'}$ with kernel $I=\mathfrak m_RB$. Its quotient isomorphism is precisely $\theta:B/I\to C$, $\bar b\mapsto q(b)$.

The module-stalk pullback lemma applied to $p,\mathcal F,x'$ gives a $C$-linear isomorphism $\beta:(\mathcal F_s)_{x'}\to M\otimes_B C$, sending $(p^*t)_{x'}$ to $t_x\otimes1$. Explicitly identify this tensor with $M/IM$: the balanced additive map $m\otimes\theta(\bar b)\mapsto\overline{bm}$ is independent of the lift $b$, since changing $b$ by an element of $I$ changes $bm$ by an element of $IM$. The balanced relation holds because $\overline{b(am)}=\overline{(ab)m}$ for $a,b\in B$. Its inverse is $\bar m\mapsto m\otimes1$: it kills $IM$ because $im\otimes1=m\otimes q(i)=0$ for $i\in I$, and the two composites are identities on classes and pure tensors, using $bm\otimes1=m\otimes q(b)$. Define $\eta(\bar m)=\beta^{-1}(m\otimes1)$. This is an additive isomorphism, and $\eta(\bar b\bar m)=\beta^{-1}(bm\otimes1)=\theta(\bar b)\eta(\bar m)$ proves the stated semilinearity. Finally the germ formula for $\beta$ gives $\eta(\overline{t_x})=(p^*t)_{x'}$ for every local section $t$. Here $IM=\mathfrak m_RM$ as defined in the statement.
